items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: you heard Rosemary Clooney sing or Bing Crosby sing or Frank Sinatra sing.

ctx.x: Everything keeps getting better and better — technology in the theater, lights and sets and all that. And maybe somehow the music was conceived as we don’t need it to be as deep as it used to be.

I don’t know. That’s a good thought. That’s certainly possible. Certainly that is a fact that things have skewed that way. Whether it’s a result or an intention I’m not in a position to judge that. I’m more inclined to think that it’s a result of the same problem that I think pop music has and that is that we reverted to cheap popular music sometime in, kind of in the middle of my lifetime, you know in my 30s and 40s. The things that had built — on which our popular music was built, going back to Stephen Foster…
and I don’t feel close to them. I don’t feel that they are — I understand their anger and their displeasure, I mean but I don’t feel connected.
